antigens.title: #41 Off-by-one in slice end
antigens.pattern: Using slice(start, start + n - 1) instead of slice(start, start + n), dropping the last item of every page

antigens.title: #57 Missing null guard on nested customer field
antigens.pattern: Reading a nested object property without an optional-chaining guard, crashing when the intermediate object is undefined or null

antigens.title: #63 Float money math
antigens.pattern: Summing currency values as IEEE 754 floats, causing rounding drift; fix is integer-cent accumulation

mutants.title: Off-by-one: start index computed one too high
mutants.description: The start index is one too high, so the first item of every page is dropped. billingCity({}) would also fail. page([1,2,3,4,5],0,2) returns [2,3] instead of [1,2].

mutants.title: Off-by-one: end index one too large, bleeds next page
mutants.description: The end index is one too large, so each page returns size+1 items. page([1,2,3,4,5],0,2) returns [1,2,3] instead of [1,2].

mutants.title: Remove optional chaining, keep fallback
mutants.description: Removes ?. so accessing .city on undefined address throws TypeError. billingCity({}) crashes instead of returning 'Unknown'.

mutants.title: Remove nullish fallback, keep optional chain
mutants.description: Removes ?? 'Unknown' so absent address returns undefined instead of 'Unknown'. billingCity({}) returns undefined, breaking equality assertions.

mutants.title: Return raw cents instead of dividing by 100
mutants.description: Drops the /100 step so the function returns cent-integers (e.g. 30 instead of 0.30). invoiceTotal([{price:0.1,qty:1},{price:0.2,qty:1}]) returns 30 instead of 0.3.

mutants.title: Accumulate floats then scale — per-item rounding lost
mutants.find: const cents = lines.reduce((sum, l) => sum + Math.round(l.price * 100) * l.qty, 0);
mutants.replace: const cents = lines.reduce((sum, l) => sum + l.price * l.qty, 0) * 100;
mutants.description: Sums raw floats first then multiplies by 100. IEEE 754 drift accumulates before scaling: (0.1+0.2)*100/100 = 0.30000000000000004, not 0.3.
